question: On 6 October 2025, the European Commission published a statement on the agreement reached between ‘the EU and Morocco to extend tariff preferences to Western Sahara’.

According to that statement, the agreement, provisionally applied since 3 October 2025, stipulates that product labels and proofs of origin have to indicate the production region (Dakhla and Laayoune) and also ensures that benefits are granted to the beneficiaries concerned in the area.

In its judgment of 4 October 2024, the Court of Justice of the European Union reaffirmed the fundamental principle that any EU act affecting the people of Western Sahara must have their consent. In accordance with that judgment: 1.
Has the consent of the people of Western Sahara been sought regarding this provisional agreement? If so, which parties were consulted?
When does the Commission expect the European Parliament to receive the relevant documents for the agreement’s ratification process?
When does the Commission expect to appear before the European Parliament?
answer: As regards the matter raised by the honorable Member of Parliament, the Commission can confirm that the new Agreement fully meets the conditions set out by the Court of Justice in its judgment of 4 October 2024 (Joined Cases C-779/21 P Commission v Front Polisario and C-799/21 P Council v Front Polisario), in particular, in paragraphs 153 et seq.

The Commission has transmitted the Commission proposals on the signature and conclusion of the new Agreement to the European Parliament. The European Parliament should also be seized by the Council with a view to obtaining its consent for the conclusion of the new Agreement. On 6 October and 4 November 2025, the Commission appeared before the European Parliament’s International Trade Committee.
The Commission stands ready to appear again and when invited by the European Parliament.
